header:
Date: 2027-03-03
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Samir Desai (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood CSM), Jenna Morales (Cobalt Head of ML), Oliver Kwan (Cobalt CTO), Priya Singh (Cobalt SRE), Ethan Brooks (Cobalt PM)
summary: Renewal check-in focused on capacity upgrade (8 -> 24 GPUs burstable), adding EU region, and contract extension. Customer leaning toward Dedicated for predictable latency; wants benchmarks in EU and clarification on data residency, KMS, and rollback policies. Next steps: pricing, benchmark, SOC2 docs, contract amendment.
topics: EU region deployment and data residency
transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll kick off in a sec, um Jenna you said you'll give a quick update on usage then we can jump into renewal items.
[00:12] Jenna: Yeah thanks Maya. So since last quarter we've seen steady growth, roughly 2.6x token volume month over month for our payments fraud flows, peak concurrency is up to about 320 concurrent requests, p95 latency on current hosted plan is around 420ms but that's US-west only, EU is still using a proxied config so it's slower.
[00:35] Oliver: Quick clarifying q, when you say p95 that's end-to-end or just generation?
[00:40] Jenna: End-to-end, includes our API gateway and some app logic, so raw inference is closer to 280-300ms on average.
[00:48] Samir: Ok got it, that matches what we saw in the report you shared, thanks. So today's agenda per the invite: renewal timing, capacity upgrade options (dedicated pools), adding EU region with data residency, and high level security requirements.
[01:05] Priya: I also want to confirm backup/rollback and audit log retention; compliance requires 7 years for some traces, that might be unique but, yeah.
[01:12] Maya: Great. On renewal, your current contract ends 2027-04-30, right?
[01:17] Ethan: Yep. We're evaluating a 12-month extension and want to add dedicated capacity in EU and bump reserved GPUs for US by end of Q2.
[01:25] Maya: Cool. We can do a 12-month amendment. Pricing will depend on committed GPU count and burst policies. Samir, can you walk through the dedicated sizing options?
[01:33] Samir: Sure. For your workload, given 320 concurrent at peaks and growth trend, our recommendation is moving from the current hosted baseline to a Dedicated pool with 8 reserved A100 equivalents with a 2x burst to 16 for spikes. If you want EU region active with similar headroom, we'd recommend a mirrored pool in eu-west-1 with at least 6 reserved and 2x burst. That would give predictable TTFB and avoid proxying across regions.
[02:00] Jenna: Does the burst allocate instantly or is there a warmup?
[02:03] Samir: Bursts are fast; there's a short allocation time for new nodes, usually within 30-90 seconds, but we also support warm pools and pre-warmed instances to keep latency flat for critical flows.
[02:12] Oliver: What's the expected p95 token latency on Dedicated with those sizes?
[02:16] Samir: For your model mix (mix of 7B and 13B quantized variants), we expect p95 generation latency around 120-180ms in-region for typical prompt lengths, end-to-end ~200-260ms. For EU we should see similar numbers if the pool is colocated.
[02:30] Priya: And cost delta vs hosted?
[02:33] Maya: Roughly you'll see higher fixed cost but lower variable per-token spend for predictable throughput. We'll share a detailed cost model in the pricing doc.
[02:40] Jenna: Another concern: can we pin model versions and have a fallback to a smaller quantized model if primary fails? We've run into noisy outputs post-upgrade before.
[02:48] Samir: Yes, rollouts and automatic fallback policies are supported. You can pin versions and configure a canary with automatic rollback if quality thresholds fail. Note transcription: sometimes our notes say 'KV cash' instead of KV cache but FYI.
[02:59] Oliver: (laughs) yeah that's the 'KV cash' problem.
[03:03] Maya: On EU deployment, data residency question — you need logs and inputs to stay in EU, right?
[03:09] Priya: Correct. All input payloads and logs need to remain in region, and KMS must be hosted by us or integrated with our key store.
[03:16] Samir: We support customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations. For private deployments we can also support an on-prem control plane or VPC peering to meet stricter requirements. For your case, a VPC deployment with customer KMS in eu-west should be doable.
[03:29] Jenna: Any limitations on audit log retention if we ask for 7 years?
[03:33] Lena: From a product standpoint we can retain logs for longer as an add-on. There may be costs and we can specify retention windows per log type. We'll include options in the SOC2 + compliance pack.
[03:44] Ethan: Can you share the SOC2 doc now?
[03:46] Maya: I'll share it after the call, plus network diagrams and the EU deployment checklist.
[03:51] Jenna: Great.
[03:53] Oliver: A small thing on routing — can we route e2e requests by policy so EU traffic hits EU pool, but US traffic still hits US pool and have an automatic fallback to hosted if Dedicated is saturated?
[04:03] Samir: Absolutely, smart routing supports region, latency and cost policies with automatic fallback to compatible model variants or hosted capacity. We'll map that in the runbook.
[04:13] Priya: For the benchmarks, we want you to run our production sample set including worst-case prompts — will that affect the SLA or capacity estimate?
[04:21] Samir: It helps refine it. If you share sample payloads and token distributions we'll run a throughput sim to calibrate. Worst-case prompts usually increase memory needs, which may push sizing up.
[04:33] Jenna: Sending that today. Also, question about tooling — we use Datadog. Is there an integration for tracing and token-level cost?
[04:41] Lena: Yes we have tracing hooks and can emit metrics to Datadog; token-level cost breakdowns and per-route dashboards are available. We'll share a sample dashboard link.
[04:52] Oliver: Competitors — we are evaluating Anthropic for safety and OpenAI for simplicity. How do you compare on rollback and deterministic outputs?
[04:59] Maya: For rollback and deterministic rollout, Redwood gives explicit eval hooks and canary gating tied to prompt sets and metrics. On deterministic outputs, models differ; we help with quantized model recommendations and evals to ensure quality doesn't regress.
[05:12] Priya: Ops question — what's the process for emergency capacity? If there's a sudden spike on a holiday can we burst beyond reserved?
[05:19] Samir: Yes, we have burst capacity and emergency provisioning with pre-agreed policies. If you need guaranteed emergency capacity we can include a paid burst buffer in the contract.
[05:29] Ethan: About contract amendment — will the dedicated pool pricing be in a separate line item? Also want to confirm termination terms if we need to downsize.
[05:37] Maya: Pricing will be line-itemed: reserved GPU commit, burst buffer, EU region mirror, plus add-ons like longer audit retention. Termination/downsize windows are typically 60 days notice for changes after a minimum commit period — we'll include options in the amendment.
[05:49] Jenna: Two quick technical clarifications: 1) do you support L4 load balancer for better sticky connection to KV cache; 2) do you support mixed model serving (13B for complex, 7B for simple) with routing?
[05:59] Samir: Yes to both. L4 keeps session affinity and helps KV cache locality. Mixed model serving is supported with request-level routing, and automatic fallback if one model is busy.
[06:10] Oliver: Any gotchas for EU deployment regarding hardware availability?
[06:14] Samir: Capacity depends on region and timing; we recommend booking commits earlier to guarantee capacity, especially for specific GPU types. We'll mark AU/EU capacity lead times in the pricing doc.
[06:24] Priya: Regarding encryption at rest, we need to ensure zero-knowledge for certain fields. Can Redwood support tokenization or field-level encryption?
[06:31] Lena: We can support field-level encryption with customer-managed keys; there are some tradeoffs for search/embeddings but for ML inference fields we can wrap those payloads. We'll detail options.
[06:44] Maya: Ok let's recap next steps. We'll send updated pricing for dedicated pools and EU mirror, include SOC2 and network diagrams, Samir will run throughput sim, and Cobalt will send traffic profile.
[06:56] Jenna: Timeline — we'd like to sign amendment by 2027-03-17 to start provisioning in early April.
[07:02] Maya: Sounds reasonable. Any final q's?
[07:06] Ethan: One last ask — can you add a clause allowing a trial of the EU mirror for 30 days with limited commitment?
[07:12] Maya: Yes we can propose a trial clause in the amendment.
[07:16] Oliver: Thanks everyone.
[07:18] Maya: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the docs and next steps.
[07:22] (call ends)

Notes: transcription has occasional mis-words, speaker overlap at times. Links referenced during call: https://redwood.app/decks/cobalt-q1 (pricing deck), SOC2/compliance pack link to be shared after call.
